requirements.text: Browser behavior a task depends on MUST be verified with `agent-browser`.
requirements.note: whether a task depends on browser behavior is not observable

requirements.text: `agent-browser upgrade` MUST run before `agent-browser` is used in a task.
requirements.note: tool invocation order within a task is not observable

requirements.text: An agent MAY discover available commands with `agent-browser --help` and command-specific usage with `agent-browser <command> --help`.
requirements.note: grants permission, so there is nothing to check

requirements.text: A commit MUST NOT use the `--no-verify` flag.
requirements.note: how git was invoked is not observable from the repository

requirements.text: Application source MUST live under `src/`.
requirements.note: flags linted JS/TS modules outside src/, exempting config files and tooling directories

requirements.text: `src/` MUST contain only the `app/`, `compositions/`, `features/`, and `shared/` folders, the root support folders, `config/`, `locales/`, and the files a framework requires at the `src` root.
requirements.note: checks src/ folder and file placement against the application structure

requirements.text: `src/features/` MUST contain only feature folders.
requirements.note: checks src/ folder and file placement against the application structure

requirements.text: A folder holding support files MUST be named `hooks/`, `types/`, `schemas/`, `constants/`, or `utils/`, matching the kind of file it holds.
requirements.note: checks src/ folder and file placement against the application structure

requirements.text: A support folder MUST NOT contain a component.
requirements.note: checks src/ folder and file placement against the application structure

requirements.text: A file that does not define a component MUST have a kebab-case name.
requirements.note: a .tsx file that defines no component is treated as a component file

requirements.text: A feature folder, `src/compositions/`, `src/shared/`, and a nested component folder MAY each contain support folders, and any other folder in these scopes MUST be a component folder containing a `.tsx` file with the same name and an `index.ts` that named-re-exports that component.
requirements.note: allows support folders in feature, compositions, shared, and nested-component scopes, and requires any other folder there to be a component folder with a same-named .tsx and an index.ts that named-re-exports it

requirements.text: A component that imports from two or more feature folders MUST live in `src/compositions/`.
requirements.note: reports a component importing from two or more feature folders

requirements.text: A component with no consumers outside `src/app/` or configuration modules, and that does not import from two or more feature folders, MUST live in the feature folder it represents or supports. If no existing feature applies, it MUST introduce a new feature folder.
requirements.note: checks the component sits under a feature folder; which feature represents it stays judgment

requirements.text: A component with at least one consumer outside `src/app/` and configuration modules MUST live in its CCF, calculated without imports from `src/app/` or configuration modules.
requirements.note: checks the component's folder against its consumers' CCF

requirements.text: When calculating a component's CCF, consumers under `src/compositions/` MUST count only when no consumer is outside `src/compositions/`.
requirements.note: checks the component's folder against its consumers' CCF

requirements.text: A component whose CCF is `src/features/` MUST live in `src/shared/`.
requirements.note: checks the component's folder against its consumers' CCF

requirements.text: `src/app/` MUST contain [Next.js App Router framework-convention files and assets](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#routing-files), plus styles required by routing files, but MUST NOT contain ordinary components or support folders.
requirements.note: checks src/ folder and file placement against the application structure

requirements.text: All configuration modules MUST live in `src/config/`.
requirements.note: checks src/ folder and file placement against the application structure

requirements.text: A configuration module MUST be one `src/config/<config-name>/` folder with `index.ts` as its entry point.
requirements.note: checks src/ folder and file placement against the application structure

requirements.text: A type, schema, or utility used only to implement one configuration module MUST be extracted even with one consumer.
requirements.note: reports a config type, schema, or utility read from outside src/config/

requirements.text: An extracted configuration type, schema, or utility MUST live in its matching dedicated folder under `src/config/<config-name>/`.
requirements.note: checks src/ folder and file placement against the application structure

requirements.text: An extracted configuration schema or utility MUST move to its matching root support folder when a consumer outside its configuration module imports it.
requirements.note: places a support file in the folder its consumers imply

requirements.text: A value MUST remain in its declaring component or file until another file imports it independently; it MUST then be extracted as a constant.
requirements.note: reports a value with cross-folder consumers not extracted

requirements.text: Extracted constants MUST live in a `constants/` folder at the CCF of their consumers.
requirements.note: places a support file in the folder its consumers imply

requirements.text: Consumers MUST import an extracted constant through the `index.ts` in that constant's `constants/` folder.
requirements.note: reports a support file imported directly instead of through the folder's index.ts

requirements.text: A `constants/` folder MUST either define its constants directly in `index.ts` or group related constants in files that `index.ts` named-re-exports.
requirements.note: reports a support folder whose index.ts does not named-re-export its files

requirements.text: When a constant's CCF is `src/features/`, it MUST move to `src/constants/`.
requirements.note: places a support file in the folder its consumers imply

requirements.text: A constant MAY live in `src/config/<module>/` instead of a `constants/` folder when a developer determines that it configures application behavior and is best understood alongside the configuration that parameterizes it, even when consumers exist outside the config module.
requirements.note: pasika/support-file-placement applies the config-module placement inside a config module, moving a constant to the consuming module; whether it configures application behavior stays a judgment

requirements.text: A file that exports values MUST use named exports unless a framework or third-party package requires a different export style for that file.
requirements.note: reports default exports where the file exports values

requirements.text: Imports MUST use whichever of the relative path and the `@/*` alias has fewer segments, counting each `../` step and each name in the path as one segment.
requirements.note: checks import paths and layer boundaries against the import rules

requirements.text: Imports MUST use the relative path when the relative path and the `@/*` alias have the same number of segments.
requirements.note: checks import paths and layer boundaries against the import rules

requirements.text: A file under `src/compositions/` MUST NOT import from `src/app/`.
requirements.note: checks import paths and layer boundaries against the import rules

requirements.text: A file in a feature folder MUST NOT import from another feature folder, `src/compositions/`, or `src/app/`.
requirements.note: checks import paths and layer boundaries against the import rules

requirements.text: A file under `src/shared/` MUST NOT import from `src/app/`, `src/compositions/`, or a feature folder.
requirements.note: checks import paths and layer boundaries against the import rules

requirements.text: A file in the `root` layer MUST NOT import from `src/app/`, `src/compositions/`, a feature folder, or `src/shared/`.
requirements.note: checks import paths and layer boundaries against the import rules

requirements.text: A configuration module MUST import only from root support folders and its own files.
requirements.note: checks import paths and layer boundaries against the import rules

requirements.text: A component MUST stay flat until it has one or more exclusive child components, then MUST be nested in a folder with the same name.
requirements.note: reports a component nested before it has exclusive children

requirements.text: A component MUST NOT be nested only because it has support files.
requirements.note: reports a component nested only because it has support files

requirements.text: A nested component's support files MUST live in its folder.
requirements.note: places a support file in the folder its consumers imply

requirements.text: The nested folder's `index.ts` MUST named-re-export the nested component and MUST NOT re-export its exclusive children.
requirements.note: reports a nested folder's index.ts not named-re-exporting the nested files

requirements.text: A custom hook MUST be extracted to its own file when two or more consumers use it.
requirements.note: reports a custom hook with two or more consumers not extracted to its own file

requirements.text: A custom hook with exactly one consumer MUST be extracted when it contains two or more imperative categories and can be described as one coherent behavior.
requirements.note: reports a hook with more imperative categories than the limit

requirements.text: An extracted custom hook MUST live in a `hooks/` folder at the CCF of its consumers.
requirements.note: places a support file in the folder its consumers imply

requirements.text: When a custom hook's CCF is `src/features/`, it MUST move to `src/hooks/`.
requirements.note: places a support file in the folder its consumers imply

requirements.text: A custom hook with one consumer that contains fewer than two imperative categories MUST stay inline in its consumer file.
requirements.note: reports a hook with more imperative categories than the limit

requirements.text: An [interactive HTML element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#interactive-content) MUST be extracted to a component with a descriptive name.
requirements.note: reports interactive elements mixed with other content without a component boundary

requirements.text: Arithmetic, chained built-in method calls, calls to functions declared outside the component, nested ternaries, and conditions containing two or more logical operators MUST be extracted before `return`, including in JSX attributes.
requirements.note: reports calculations and complex conditions inside JSX children and attributes

requirements.text: An inline expression MAY contain one condition with up to one logical operator, one ternary, or one built-in method call. `cn()` MAY be called inline. An event handler MAY make one call inline.
requirements.note: the jsx-hygiene check flags every expression outside this set, so exactly these stay inline

requirements.text: All locales MUST live in the named `locales` object exported from `src/locales/index.ts`.
requirements.note: reports a locale not living in the named locales object

requirements.text: Locales read only by files in one feature folder MUST live in an object with the camelCase form of its feature folder name (for example, `user-settings` becomes `userSettings`).
requirements.note: checks the folder a locale's consumers imply

requirements.text: Locales read by files in more than one feature folder or by `src/shared/`, `src/compositions/`, `src/app/`, or root support folders MUST live at the top level of `locales`.
requirements.note: checks the folder a locale's consumers imply

requirements.text: A namespaced locale MUST be read through its full dotted path (`locales.stream.watchLiveStream`).
requirements.note: reports a namespaced locale read through a path other than its full dotted path

requirements.text: A locale key MUST be camelCase English based on the text. A direct translation longer than 30 characters is unwieldy, so such a key MUST describe the message's purpose instead and end in a WAI-ARIA element role postfix such as Button, Link, or Dialog. A shorter key MAY describe the message's purpose instead when the direct translation would be unclear.
requirements.note: the locale-key-shape check enforces camelCase and requires keys over 30 characters to end in a WAI-ARIA element role; whether a short key reads as its text stays judgment

requirements.text: A block of elements SHOULD be extracted to a component when one clear name describes the whole block.
requirements.note: deciding one clear name describes a block is a naming judgment

requirements.text: A `.tsx` file that defines a component MUST contain exactly one component.
requirements.note: counts exported components; a second component that is not exported is not detected

requirements.text: A block of elements MUST be extracted as a named component when two or more places use the same arrangement of elements for the same purpose. Different data or labels do not prevent extraction.
requirements.note: compares sibling JSX blocks for identical markup, ignoring text and expression data

requirements.text: A smart component file name MUST be `PascalCase.tsx`.
requirements.note: checks file names against the PascalCase/kebab-case conventions

requirements.text: A dumb component file name MUST be `kebab-case.tsx`.
requirements.note: checks file names against the PascalCase/kebab-case conventions

requirements.text: A smart component with one outer DOM element in every rendered result MUST set `data-testid` on that element, and its value MUST match the component name in `PascalCase`.
requirements.note: checks data-testid values where a rendered result carries one

requirements.text: A smart component MUST render exactly one outer DOM element in every rendered result, and MUST set `data-testid` on it; a smart component with no single outer element MUST wrap its content in one instead of rendering multiple roots.
requirements.note: reports a smart component whose rendered result has no single outer element, requiring one wrapping element with the data-testid

requirements.text: A dumb component MAY set `data-testid` on its root element, and the value MUST be `kebab-case`.
requirements.note: checks data-testid values where a rendered result carries one

requirements.text: [Next.js App Router routing files](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#routing-files) MUST use their required kebab-case names and are exempt from smart/dumb file-name and `data-testid` requirements.
requirements.note: checks data-testid values where a rendered result carries one

requirements.text: A component MUST extract a named component when one part of its JSX contains every JSX expression, callback, and effect that reads one state hook's value or calls its updater.
requirements.note: finds a useState hook read and its updater called only inside JSX, all within one contiguous run of the returned JSX's top-level children with a sibling that never touches it; whether the part reads only that hook stays judgment

requirements.text: A type or schema declared in a component MUST stay in that component file until another file imports it without the component where it is defined.
requirements.note: reports a type or schema with cross-folder consumers not extracted

requirements.text: Importing a type or schema alongside the component that defines it MUST NOT require extraction.
requirements.note: the type-extraction check only requires extraction when a consumer imports the type without the defining component, so importing it alongside the component never fires

requirements.text: A type or schema declared outside a component MUST stay in its file until another file needs it without using the code in that file.
requirements.note: reports a type or schema with cross-folder consumers not extracted

requirements.text: Extracted types and schemas MUST live in their matching `types/` or `schemas/` folder at the CCF of their consumers.
requirements.note: places a support file in the folder its consumers imply

requirements.text: When a type or schema's CCF is `src/features/`, it MUST move to `src/types/` or `src/schemas/`.
requirements.note: places a support file in the folder its consumers imply

requirements.text: A `types/` or `schemas/` folder MUST either define its exports directly in `index.ts` or group related types and schemas in files that `index.ts` named-re-exports.
requirements.note: reports a support folder whose index.ts does not named-re-export its files

requirements.text: Consumers MUST import an extracted type or schema through the `index.ts` in that type or schema's `types/` or `schemas/` folder.
requirements.note: reports a support file imported directly instead of through the folder's index.ts

requirements.text: A type or schema used only to implement one configuration module MUST live in that module's `types/` or `schemas/` folder.
requirements.note: places a support file in the folder its consumers imply

requirements.text: A type MAY stay in `src/config/<module>/` when its meaning is derived from the configuration that it parameterizes, even when consumers exist outside the config module.
requirements.note: pasika/support-file-placement applies the config-module placement inside a config module, moving a type to the consuming module; whether its meaning derives from the configuration stays a judgment

requirements.text: A pure function MUST be extracted to `utils/`, even when it has one consumer.
requirements.note: reports a pure function with consumers not extracted to utils/

requirements.text: An extracted utility MUST live in the `utils/` folder at the CCF of its consumers.
requirements.note: places a support file in the folder its consumers imply

requirements.text: When a utility's CCF is `src/features/`, it MUST move to `src/utils/`.
requirements.note: places a support file in the folder its consumers imply

requirements.text: A utility MUST be imported directly without a barrel.
requirements.note: reports a utility imported through a barrel

requirements.text: A utility file that exports one function MUST have a name in that function's kebab-case form.
requirements.note: reports a single-function utility file not named in the function's kebab-case form

requirements.text: Utilities that are used together MAY be grouped in one file.
requirements.note: grants permission, so there is nothing to check

requirements.text: A utility used only to implement one configuration module MUST live in that module's `utils/` folder.
requirements.note: places a support file in the folder its consumers imply

requirements.text: Each How To step MUST be concise and use one sentence.
requirements.note: one sentence is checked; whether it is concise is judgment

requirements.text: A Guide MAY link Rules, References, Policy documents, and other Guides.
requirements.note: the no-cross-document-link check exempts guide files, so a Guide may link Rules, References, Policy documents, and other Guides

requirements.text: A Guide overview MUST contain one or two short descriptive sentences about the guide's scope and purpose, and MUST NOT contain instructions or links to other documentation.
requirements.note: docs-check: an overview must contain one or two short sentences and must not link

requirements.text: Each How To step MUST link at most one documentation file total, whatever kind that file is.
requirements.note: docs-check: each How To step links at most one documentation file

requirements.text: When a step links another document, the step MUST name the concrete decision or result the reader will have after reading it.
requirements.note: whether a step names a concrete result is a reading judgment

requirements.text: A step that links another Guide MUST link directly to the relevant How To section.
requirements.note: docs-check: a guide link carries a How To anchor

requirements.text: How To sections MUST NOT nest inside other How To sections.
requirements.note: docs-check: no heading nests inside a How To section

requirements.text: Guide file names MUST match the document title in kebab-case and use the `-guide` suffix (e.g., `foo-guide.md`).
requirements.note: docs-check: file names match the document title and carry the kind suffix

requirements.text: A Guide with support files MUST become a folder named the same as its entry-point file, without the `.md` extension.
requirements.note: docs-check: a Guide with support files must be a folder named like the guide

requirements.text: A Rule file that a Guide owns MUST live in a `rules/` subfolder inside the Guide's folder.
requirements.note: docs-check: a Guide-owned Rule/Reference must live in the matching subfolder

requirements.text: A Reference file that a Guide owns MUST live in a `references/` subfolder inside the Guide's folder.
requirements.note: docs-check: a Guide-owned Rule/Reference must live in the matching subfolder

requirements.text: A Guide whose steps use terms that a glossary Reference defines MUST link that Reference from its first step.
requirements.note: docs-check: compare glossary terms against the guide's steps

requirements.text: Policy file names MUST match the document title in kebab-case and use the `-policy` suffix (e.g., `foo-policy.md`).
requirements.note: docs-check: file names match the document title and carry the kind suffix

requirements.text: A Policy overview MUST contain one or two short sentences naming the scope the requirements apply to.
requirements.note: docs-check: an overview must contain one or two short sentences

requirements.text: A Policy document MUST state requirements that apply to the whole repository and span two or more unrelated subjects.
requirements.note: deciding subjects are unrelated enough to share one document is an editorial call

requirements.text: A Policy document MUST state every requirement as a bullet that uses RFC 2119 vocabulary.
requirements.note: docs-check: the document must state requirements as bullets using RFC 2119 vocabulary

requirements.text: A Policy document MUST group its bullets under a heading per subject.
requirements.note: docs-check: every bullet sits under a subject heading

requirements.text: A Policy document MUST NOT contain Incorrect/Correct examples, and a requirement that a reader cannot apply without one MUST live in a Rule instead.
requirements.note: docs-check: a Policy document must not contain Incorrect/Correct examples

requirements.text: A Policy document MUST NOT link to Rules, References, Guides, or other Policy documents.
requirements.note: docs-check: a document of this kind must not link to those other kinds

requirements.text: Reference file names MUST match the document title in kebab-case and use the `-reference` suffix (e.g., `foo-reference.md`).
requirements.note: docs-check: file names match the document title and carry the kind suffix

requirements.text: A Reference MUST NOT link to Rules, Guides, Policy documents, or other References.
requirements.note: docs-check: a document of this kind must not link to those other kinds

requirements.text: A Reference MUST NOT use RFC 2119 vocabulary (`MUST`, `MUST NOT`, `SHOULD`, `SHOULD NOT`, `MAY`), because lookup material describes what exists rather than imposing requirements.
requirements.note: docs-check: a Reference must not use RFC 2119 vocabulary

requirements.text: A Reference MUST NOT state a constraint the reader has to satisfy, even in plain declarative wording, and a constraint the reader has to satisfy MUST live in a Rule.
requirements.note: recognizing a constraint stated as description requires reading it as a reader would

requirements.text: A Reference MAY define terms that Rules, Guides, and Policy documents use.
requirements.note: grants permission, so there is nothing to check

requirements.text: A Reference MAY name an RFC 2119 keyword as lookup content, because naming a keyword does not impose a requirement.
requirements.note: docs-check reference-no-rfc-vocabulary ignores code spans

requirements.text: A Reference overview and the overview of each headed lookup block MUST contain one or two short sentences.
requirements.note: docs-check: an overview must contain one or two short sentences

requirements.text: A Reference with a single lookup block MUST NOT add a section heading for it.
requirements.note: docs-check: Reference lookup blocks must follow the heading rules

requirements.text: A Reference with two or more lookup blocks MUST add a section heading for every block, including the first.
requirements.note: docs-check: Reference lookup blocks must follow the heading rules

requirements.text: Rule file names MUST match the document title in kebab-case and use the `-rule` suffix (e.g., `foo-rule.md`).
requirements.note: docs-check: file names match the document title and carry the kind suffix

requirements.text: A Rule overview MUST contain one or two short sentences naming the problem the rule solves.
requirements.note: docs-check: an overview must contain one or two short sentences

requirements.text: A Rule MUST state requirements about one subject.
requirements.note: deciding requirements share one subject is an editorial call

requirements.text: A Rule MUST contain at least one bullet point that uses [RFC 2119 vocabulary](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2119) (`MUST`, `MUST NOT`, `SHOULD`, `SHOULD NOT`, `MAY`).
requirements.note: docs-check: the document must state requirements as bullets using RFC 2119 vocabulary

requirements.text: RFC 2119 vocabulary MUST appear only in bullet points, so the bullet list is the single place a requirement is stated.
requirements.note: docs-check: RFC 2119 vocabulary appears only in bullets

requirements.text: A bullet MUST use `MUST` or `MUST NOT` only when the requirement admits no exception, and `SHOULD` or `SHOULD NOT` only when exceptions are possible.
requirements.note: matching a keyword's strength to the requirement's intent is a reading judgment

requirements.text: Prose outside bullet points — intros, `Why:` explanations, table cells, and code comments — MUST restate a requirement in plain language instead of repeating RFC 2119 vocabulary.
requirements.note: docs-check: RFC 2119 vocabulary appears only in bullets

requirements.text: A bullet MUST NOT define a term, and a term a reader needs in order to apply the Rule MUST be defined in a Reference instead.
requirements.note: recognizing a bullet as a definition rather than a demand is a reading judgment

requirements.text: A Rule MUST contain at least one Incorrect/Correct pair.
requirements.note: docs-check: a Rule must contain at least one Incorrect/Correct pair

requirements.text: A Rule MAY contain multiple Incorrect/Correct pairs.
requirements.note: grants permission, so there is nothing to check

requirements.text: An Incorrect/Correct pair MUST add a concise description after an em dash in both headings, so readers can scan the examples by decision.
requirements.note: docs-check: an Incorrect/Correct pair must add a concise description

requirements.text: A Rule MUST NOT link to References, Guides, or other Rules.
requirements.note: docs-check: a document of this kind must not link to those other kinds

requirements.text: Authors MUST start from the template that matches the chosen document kind and structure.
requirements.note: which template an author started from is not recorded in the result

requirements.text: Authors MUST replace each bracketed prompt with the final title, explanation, step, or lookup content it asks for.
requirements.note: docs-check: a bracketed template prompt must be replaced

requirements.text: Authors MUST delete template branches that do not apply to the document being written.
requirements.note: an unused branch is only recognizable by comparing against the template

requirements.text: Documentation support assets MAY live in folders whose names start with an underscore.
requirements.note: the documentation parser skips folders whose names start with an underscore

requirements.text: Runtime validation MUST use Zod schemas rather than ad hoc type guards.
requirements.note: flags hand-written type predicates over unknown/any that don't delegate to a schema; as-casts and inline manual checks are not detected

requirements.text: A data contract's fields MUST be required unless runtime evidence shows they are optional or nullable.
requirements.note: deciding a field is genuinely optional requires evidence about runtime data

requirements.text: A change MUST update every in-repo call site rather than preserve backward compatibility, unless the user asks for compatibility.
requirements.note: recognizing a compatibility shim requires knowing the change's intent

requirements.text: Code MUST NOT use `eslint-disable` directives, and a reported violation MUST be fixed instead.
requirements.note: reports eslint-disable directives

requirements.text: A lint command MUST NOT pass ESLint's `--cache` flag, because rules that compare a file against the rest of the tree need every file in the run.
requirements.note: reports lint scripts passing --cache

requirements.text: A repository MUST take its lint, format, and TypeScript configuration from `pasika` and `zirka` rather than restating it locally.
requirements.note: pasika doctor checks the eslint config and tsconfig against the pasika/zirka baseline

requirements.text: Documentation written outside this repository MUST be consumed through Vulyk rather than copied in.
requirements.note: recognizing a document as copied from elsewhere is not decidable from the repository

requirements.text: A change to the Vulyk registry MUST use Vulyk commands rather than edits to generated files.
requirements.note: pasika doctor warns when a file listed in the .vulyk manifest is newer than it

requirements.text: A file listed in a `.vulyk` manifest MUST NOT be edited by hand.
requirements.note: pasika doctor warns when a file listed in the .vulyk manifest is newer than it

requirements.text: Vulyk MUST run as an ephemeral command such as `npx vulyk@latest`.
requirements.note: reports vulyk in package.json dependencies instead of run ephemerally

requirements.text: Vulyk MUST NOT be added to `package.json` in order to run its CLI.
requirements.note: reports vulyk in package.json dependencies instead of run ephemerally

requirements.text: Components MUST NOT use arbitrary-value classes for project styling. They MUST use an existing Tailwind or project utility, or define a project token or custom utility first.
requirements.note: reports arbitrary-value classes for project-specific values

requirements.text: Components MUST use `cn` or the project's equivalent class-merging helper for conditional classes and a `className` passed to the component.
requirements.note: detects + and template literals; a conditional expression without cn is not detected

requirements.text: Components MUST NOT concatenate class strings with template literals or `+` when any part is conditional.
requirements.note: reports class strings concatenated or props that should use cn()/CVA

requirements.text: A `className` passed to a component MUST contain only outer-layout utilities: margins, sizing, flex or grid item placement, and `z-index`.
requirements.note: reports class strings concatenated or props that should use cn()/CVA

requirements.text: A component MUST expose its supported appearance and size variants through typed props, not through a passed `className` or separate class-name props for internal elements.
requirements.note: reports class strings concatenated or props that should use cn()/CVA

requirements.text: A static class list with more than five class names MUST use `cn` with multiple string literals, each grouped by styling concern and containing no more than five class names.
requirements.note: reports class strings concatenated or props that should use cn()/CVA

requirements.text: A component MUST own a distinguishable appearance for every UI state it supports.
requirements.note: whether every supported state looks distinguishable is a visual judgment

requirements.text: A component MUST use Tailwind "state variants" when they can express a supported UI state.
requirements.note: reports a UI state not expressed through native state or Tailwind state variants

requirements.text: A component MUST express a UI state through the native element, attribute, or ARIA state for it and MUST NOT use a custom equivalent.
requirements.note: reports a UI state not expressed through native state or Tailwind state variants

requirements.text: A component that lets callers choose visual options MUST define them with `cva`.
requirements.note: reports a component that does not define its visual options as CVA variant props

requirements.text: A component's variant prop types MUST be derived from its `cva` definition with `VariantProps` rather than manually duplicated unions.
requirements.note: reports variant prop types not derived from the cva variants

requirements.text: A boolean prop that changes appearance MUST use conditional `cn()` when it only adds or removes one standalone class treatment.
requirements.note: reports a boolean appearance prop not expressed through conditional variants

requirements.text: A boolean prop that changes appearance MUST use a CVA variant when both boolean values have explicit treatments or when the boolean participates in a compound variant.
requirements.note: reports a boolean appearance prop not expressed through conditional variants

requirements.text: A repository MUST have one global stylesheet entry point that registers Tailwind.
requirements.note: pasika doctor checks the repository has a global stylesheet registering Tailwind

requirements.text: The project's global CSS MUST live in the global stylesheet entry point and MUST NOT be imported from another file.
requirements.note: reports the global CSS outside the required stylesheet entry point

requirements.text: The global stylesheet MUST reset Tailwind's default theme with `--*: initial`.
requirements.note: reports a missing --*: initial theme reset in the global stylesheet

requirements.text: Every value used for the project's styling MUST be defined as a CSS variable in `:root`, even when no theme selector overrides it. A Tailwind theme variable MUST reference that CSS variable through `@theme inline`.
requirements.note: reports a styling value not defined as a root CSS custom property

requirements.text: Style declarations added by the project inside global selectors MUST use `@apply`.
requirements.note: reports @apply missing for declarations the rule requires in the base layer

requirements.text: The global stylesheet MUST order imports, `@custom-variant` definitions, `:root` variables and the selectors that override them, `@theme` definitions, custom utilities, base styles, and keyframes in that order.
requirements.note: reports stylesheet sections out of the required order

requirements.text: The global base layer MUST apply `base-canvas` and `base-ink` to the document body as the default page pair.
requirements.note: reports a base layer that does not apply base-canvas and base-ink

requirements.text: Styling used by only one component MUST stay in that component file as static Tailwind utility classes and MUST NOT be moved to the global stylesheet.
requirements.note: reports a style shared by two or more components not extracted to a named utility

requirements.text: A style or group of styles that two or more components use together and should change together MUST become one named custom utility. The group MAY include utilities generated by theme variables, built-in utilities, other custom utilities, and interaction styles.
requirements.note: reports a style shared by two or more components not extracted to a named utility

requirements.text: A value that needs at least two utility classes from the same [Tailwind theme-variable namespace](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/theme#theme-variable-namespaces) MUST use that namespace and have the same name in `:root`.
requirements.note: reports a utility class group not sharing a namespace prefix

requirements.text: A CSS variable intended only for a background MUST be named `--<role>-canvas`, and one intended only for readable text MUST be named `--<role>-ink`. When a named custom utility exposes one of those values by itself, it MUST use `bg-<role>-canvas` or `text-<role>-ink`.
requirements.note: reports a CSS variable named against the wrong canvas/ink convention

requirements.text: A repeated combination of canvas, ink, and related styles MUST become a `*-surface` custom Tailwind utility that owns the combination.
requirements.note: reports a repeated canvas+ink combo not extracted to a named surface utility

requirements.text: A custom utility MUST use `@apply` for every styling declaration added by the project. When no named built-in utility represents a property value, it MUST apply the Tailwind custom-property or arbitrary-property utility instead.
requirements.note: reports a custom utility that does not use @apply for its styling declarations
